name: tui-vpn
tagline: WireGuard and its control plane, from the terminal
description:
WireGuard from the terminal, together with the self-hosted control plane that decides who is allowed onto it.

The status screen reads your interfaces straight from `wg show all dump`: peers, endpoints, handshakes, transfer, allowed IPs and keepalive. Creating an interface from zero, up/down, adding or removing a peer, saving the runtime config — every change is previewed as the exact command line and applied only after you confirm it. A private key is never shown, typed, or put on a command line: keys are generated by a root shell straight into root-only files, the conf references the key file instead of inlining it, and a pre-shared key reaches `wg` as a file path, never as an argument.

When a [Headscale](https://headscale.net) control plane is present, tui-vpn also manages users, nodes and pre-auth keys — a created pre-auth key is shown exactly once and never stored — under the same rule. Identity is OpenID Connect in the client's browser against your IdP; the server exposes no web admin, by design.

Run it with `--demo` to see every screen with nothing installed.

screenshots.caption: The status screen: WireGuard interfaces, their state and peer counts, read from wg
The peers screen: endpoints, handshake age and transfer for the selected interface
The Headscale nodes screen: who owns each node and its state, above the OIDC identity note
The help screen: keys, and how identity works over OIDC

keys.action: Switch screen (interfaces, peers, users, nodes, keys)
Create a new interface from zero (keygen, conf, optional up)
Bring the selected interface up / down
Save the interface's runtime config (wg-quick save)
Add / remove a peer on the interface (add: optional pre-shared key file)
Create a Headscale user (users screen) or pre-auth key (keys screen)
Expire / rename / delete the selected node

notes.impact: `preauthkeys list` requires a `--user`, so the pre-auth keys screen may be empty; users and nodes are unaffected

source.command:
git clone https://github.com/tui-tools/tui-vpn
cd tui-vpn && make demo

pacman.note: Available once the first release lands in pkgs.tui.tools.

apt.note: Available once the first release lands in pkgs.tui.tools.

dnf.note: Available once the first release lands in pkgs.tui.tools.

binary.command:
curl -fsSL https://github.com/tui-tools/tui-vpn/releases/download/v{version}/tui-vpn_{version}_linux_{arch}.tar.gz | tar -xz tui-vpn
sudo install -m0755 tui-vpn /usr/local/bin/tui-vpn
binary.note: Available once the first release is tagged.

security.needs_sudo: Reading a WireGuard interface needs CAP_NET_ADMIN and the Headscale CLI talks to a root-owned socket, so reads escalate through the configured prefix; `ip link` does not. Every mutation escalates and is previewed and confirmed first.
